## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Chinese rendering of the **Mūlasarvāstivāda *bhikṣu-prātimokṣa*** (249 rules), drawn from the parent Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya *bhikṣu-vibhaṅga* ([KR6k0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0023)). Translated by **Yìjìng** ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8)) in the early 8th century. This is the standard recitation-text used in Tibetan Buddhist monasteries.

**Abstract**

The Mūlasarvāstivāda *prātimokṣa* in 249 rules is the **Vinaya** of all Tibetan, Mongolian, and Bhutanese Buddhist monasticism — every Tibetan *bhikṣu* ordained in the Mūlasarvāstivāda lineage uses some Tibetan recension descended from this text. The Sanskrit version is well preserved in the Gilgit manuscripts (Banerjee 1957, 1977). Comparative philological work (Prebish 1975) shows the Mūlasarvāstivāda *prātimokṣa* to be substantively close to the older Sarvāstivāda ([KR6k0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0017)) but with school-specific divergences in several *naiḥsargika* and *pāyantika* rules.
